---
title: "Compare CBS Carbon Intensities"
output:
  html_document:
    df_print: paged
---

This notebook compares different methods to calculate carbon intensities for each CBS product.

- **preRAS**: Divide the total CBS GHG emissions by the desired CBS column sums (total expenditures according to CBS) in different years (2014-2016)
- **postRAS**: Divide the total CBS GHG emissions by the actual CBS column sums after performing the RAS (total expenditures according to CBS product-wisely scaled to EXIOBASE).

If the carbon intensity of a product is different in one method compared to the other, it indicates that

- Carbon intensity is **lower** in *postRAS* than in *preRAS*: EXIOBASE estimates higher expenditures than CBS
- Carbon intensity is **higher** in *postRAS* than in *preRAS*: EXIOBASE estimates smaller expenditures than CBS

```{r, setup, include = F}
# R version 4.2.3 (2023-03-15 ucrt)

knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir = '..', scipen = 999)

library(tidyverse)  # Version 2.0.0
library(readxl) # Version 1.4.2
```


```{r readData, include = FALSE}
# Read data
df_preRAS_2014 <- read_excel("CorrespondenceTables_CBS-EXIOBASE_preRAS_2014.xlsx", sheet = "CarbonIntensity_CBS")
df_preRAS_2015 <- read_excel("CorrespondenceTables_CBS-EXIOBASE_preRAS_2015.xlsx", sheet = "CarbonIntensity_CBS")
df_preRAS_2016 <- read_excel("CorrespondenceTables_CBS-EXIOBASE_preRAS_2016.xlsx", sheet = "CarbonIntensity_CBS")
df_postRAS_2015 <- read_excel("CorrespondenceTables_CBS-EXIOBASE_final.xlsx", sheet = "CarbonIntensity_CBS")


emissions_preRAS_2014 <- read_excel("CorrespondenceTables_CBS-EXIOBASE_preRAS_2014.xlsx", sheet = "CarbonEmissions_CBS")
emissions_preRAS_2015 <- read_excel("CorrespondenceTables_CBS-EXIOBASE_preRAS_2015.xlsx", sheet = "CarbonEmissions_CBS")
emissions_preRAS_2016 <- read_excel("CorrespondenceTables_CBS-EXIOBASE_preRAS_2016.xlsx", sheet = "CarbonEmissions_CBS")
emissions_postRAS_2015 <- read_excel("CorrespondenceTables_CBS-EXIOBASE_final.xlsx", sheet = "CarbonEmissions_CBS")

expenditures <- read_excel("CorrespondenceTables_CBS-EXIOBASE_final.xlsx", sheet = "Expenditures_CBS")
```

```{r make_df function, include = F}
make_df <- function(regexpression, exp = 1){
  vars <- df_postRAS_2015$Variable[which(grepl(regexpression, df_postRAS_2015$Variable))]
  
  new_df_intensities <- data.frame("product" = 
                        df_postRAS_2015$Product[which(df_postRAS_2015$Variable %in% vars)],
                      "intensity_preRAS_2014" = 
                        df_preRAS_2014$CarbonIntensity[which(df_preRAS_2014$Variable %in% vars)] * exp, 
                      "intensity_preRAS_2015" = 
                        df_preRAS_2015$CarbonIntensity[which(df_preRAS_2015$Variable %in% vars)] * exp, 
                      "intensity_preRAS_2016" = 
                        df_preRAS_2016$CarbonIntensity[which(df_preRAS_2016$Variable %in% vars)] * exp, 
                      "intensity_postRAS_2015" = 
                        df_postRAS_2015$CarbonIntensity[which(df_postRAS_2015$Variable %in% vars)] * exp)
  
  print(summary(new_df_intensities))
  

  new_df_totalEmissions <- data.frame("product" = df_postRAS_2015$Product,
                    "emissions_preRAS_2014" = df_preRAS_2014$CarbonIntensity * expenditures$Expenditures, 
                    "emissions_preRAS_2015" = df_preRAS_2015$CarbonIntensity * expenditures$Expenditures, 
                    "emissions_preRAS_2016" = df_preRAS_2016$CarbonIntensity * expenditures$Expenditures, 
                    "emissions_postRAS_2015" = df_postRAS_2015$CarbonIntensity * expenditures$Expenditures)
  
  print(summary(new_df_totalEmissions))
  
  new_df_expenditures <- data.frame("product" = 
                        expenditures$Product[which(expenditures$Variable %in% vars)],
                        "expenditures" = expenditures$Expenditures[which(expenditures$Variable %in% vars)])
  
  print(summary(new_df_expenditures))
  
  new_df <- merge(new_df_intensities, new_df_totalEmissions, by = "product")
  new_df <- merge(new_df, new_df_expenditures, by = "product")
  
  return(new_df)
}
```

```{r make dataframes, include = F}
df_all <- make_df("")
df_all <- df_all[match(df_postRAS_2015$Product, df_all$product), ] # reorder according to the initial order
rownames(df_all) <- NULL

df_food <- make_df("BOBEST01")
df_drinks <- make_df("BOBEST02")
df_clothes <- make_df("BOBEST03")
df_accomodation <- make_df("BOBEST04")
df_household <- make_df("BOBEST05")
df_transport <- make_df("BOBEST07")
df_officeSupplies <- make_df("BOBEST08")
df_freeTime <- make_df("BOBEST09")

```


```{r make_plot function, include = F}
# Reshape the data frame to long format
make_plot <- function(df, title, intensity_limits = NA, emissions_limits = NA, expenditure_limits = NA, save = FALSE){
  
  ### carbon intensities ###
  df_long <- df %>%
    pivot_longer(cols = c(intensity_preRAS_2014, intensity_preRAS_2015, intensity_preRAS_2016, intensity_postRAS_2015),
                 names_to = "method",
                 values_to = "intensity")  
  
  df_long$method <- factor(df_long$method, levels = c("intensity_preRAS_2016", "intensity_preRAS_2015", "intensity_preRAS_2014", "intensity_postRAS_2015"))
  
  # Reorder levels of product based on newMethod values
  df_long$product <- factor(df_long$product, 
                            levels = unique(
                              df_long$product[which(df_long$method == "intensity_postRAS_2015")]
                              [order(df_long$intensity[which(df_long$method == "intensity_postRAS_2015")])]))
  
  desired_order <- levels(df_long$product)
  
  plot_intensity <- ggplot(df_long, aes(x = product, y = intensity, fill = method)) +
    geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = "dodge") +
    labs(x = "Product", y = "Carbon Intensity") +
    scale_fill_manual(values = c("darkolivegreen", "darkolivegreen4", "darkolivegreen3", "burlywood2")) +
    guides(fill = guide_legend(reverse = T)) +
    theme_minimal() +
    ggtitle(title)
    
  if(length(intensity_limits) > 1){
    plot_intensity <- plot_intensity + scale_y_continuous(limits = c(intensity_limits))
  }
  
  plot_intensity <- plot_intensity + coord_flip()
  
  if(save){
    ggsave(paste("plots/", title, "_intensity.png", sep = ""), width = 7, height = 4)
  }
  
  print(plot_intensity)
  
  
  
  ### carbon emissions ###
  df_long <- df %>%
    pivot_longer(cols = c(emissions_preRAS_2014, emissions_preRAS_2015, emissions_preRAS_2016, emissions_postRAS_2015),
                 names_to = "method",
                 values_to = "emissions")  
  
  df_long$method <- factor(df_long$method, levels = c("emissions_preRAS_2016", "emissions_preRAS_2015", "emissions_preRAS_2014", "emissions_postRAS_2015"))
  
  # Reorder levels of product based on the newMethod values of carbon intensity (as above)
  df_long$product <- factor(df_long$product, levels = desired_order)
  
  
  plot_emissions <- ggplot(df_long, aes(x = product, y = emissions, fill = method)) +
    geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = "dodge") +
    labs(x = "Product", y = "Carbon Emissions") +
    scale_fill_manual(values = c("darkolivegreen", "darkolivegreen4", "darkolivegreen3", "burlywood2")) +
    guides(fill = guide_legend(reverse = T)) +
    theme_minimal() +
    ggtitle(title)
    
  if(length(emissions_limits) > 1){
    plot_emissions <- plot_emissions + scale_y_continuous(limits = c(emissions_limits))
  }
  
  plot_emissions <- plot_emissions + coord_flip()
  
  if(save){
    ggsave(paste("plots/", title, "_emissions.png", sep = ""), width = 7, height = 4)
  }
  
  print(plot_emissions)
  
  
  
  ### expenditures ###
  
  # Reorder levels of product based on the newMethod values of carbon intensity (as above)
  df$product <- factor(df$product, levels = desired_order)
  
  plot_expenditures <- ggplot(df, aes(x = product, y = expenditures)) +
    geom_bar(stat = "identity", fill = "darkolivegreen") + 
    labs(x = "Product", y = "Expenditures") +
    guides(fill = guide_legend(reverse = T)) +
    theme_minimal() +
    ggtitle(title)
  
  if(length(expenditure_limits) > 1){
    plot_expenditures <- plot_expenditures + scale_y_continuous(limits = c(expenditure_limits))
  }
  
  plot_expenditures <- plot_expenditures + coord_flip()
  
  print(plot_expenditures)
  
  if(save){
    ggsave(paste("plots/", title, "_expenditures.png", sep = ""), width = 7, height = 4)
  }
}
```

## Education

What seems to be happening here is that according to EXIOBASE, households spend less money on education than according to CBS. Therefore, the denominator in *newMethod* is smaller and thus the carbon intensity is higher.
